x: They finished in that order with times of 57:31,58:26,and 60:19. Cecil Mains was 4th, Tom Carter 5th and Harry Shields 6th.

Things were sorted out and the 80 year old turned out to be Cecil Mains (not to be confused with Dave) who was a cross-country man and my records show him as finishing 4th to Bert Footer, Arthur Penny and Arthur Allum in the 1933 10 miles Club Cross-Country Championship.

C. Mains, a young man of twenty, running his first race for us … did very well over what is, perhaps, the most difficult stage of the lot … the gradual ascent of the South Downs, culminating in the climb of Dale Hill.
